newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India sees some buying as BSE holds.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India sees some buying as BSE holds.

text.p: There was some tentative buying in Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) as the Bombay share index held above the 3,000 level.

"There were buyers for some very cheap stocks, not a lot, but Larsen & Toubro, which hit a discount to the underlying for the first time ever yesterday bounced back to a 10 percent premium," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.79 points, or 1.35 percent, at 59.49 points, with the premium over the local market at 9.90 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 10.28 points, or 0.34 percent, to 3037.63. "The downside now looks to be in the order of 200 points, not more," said a trader.
L&T closed up 60 cents at $12.25/$13.25, Bajaj Auto added 82 cents $20.00/$21.00 and Hindalco was up 77 to $16.50/$17.50.
"The market feels okay, although I would not want to get carried away yet," said the trader.

Rate cut talk drove the Capel Korea GDR Index 2.07 points, or 4.17 percent higher, to 71.00, a premium of 26.81 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 2.53 percent, or 20.16 points, to close provisionally at 817.78.
Korea, which had been sold down over the past month, was also boosted by a positive North American book-to-bill ratio; at 0.99 in September, the ratio was the highest level this year.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.27 points at 91.32, a premium of 2.85 percent over the locals after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 2.95 points, or 0.04 percent, to 6,587.86.
"Taiwan is taking a bit of a breather," said an Asia trader.
